decision.message:
URGENT – electrical safety – 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ (tenant Nora Bell; landlord Elliot Vane).

What is wrong: at 08:14 today the tenant reported a hot, slightly burning smell at the kitchen counter socket. The socket face felt warm after a kettle had been plugged in (E001). At 16:42 the faint smell is still there near the counter (E025). Nobody has reported smoke, sparks or flame. The kettle is unplugged and the socket has not been used since. Nobody has switched off a breaker, the fridge is still on, and we do not know which circuit the socket is on (E008, E025). Her 10-year-old son lives at the flat and was there this morning (E004).

What has been tried: the landlord sent his general handyman, Rowan Pike. Rowan does not do fixed-wiring work and has no electrical test equipment (E011, E015). He did not go in because nobody answered and he had no clear permission to enter, so there has been no inspection and no isolation (E019, E023). We called the landlord at 13:14 and got voicemail (E020). We emailed him at 15:02 asking for an immediate decision, with no reply (E024). His only instructions so far are for the handyman to look and report, and to keep costs down. He has not approved an electrician (E006, E016, E021). The tenant says she has had no safety guidance from us (E009, E025). I am sending her interim safety advice and texting the landlord in this same turn.

Decisions needed from you today:
1. Phone Elliot Vane now for authority to send a qualified (registered) electrician out today to make the socket and circuit safe and assess it, including any out-of-hours cost.
2. If he cannot be reached, decide whether Northbridge will get an electrician out under its own emergency or out-of-hours arrangements, and on what cost basis.
3. Confirm access. The tenant is home now, so landlord-held keys should not be needed tonight.

Please confirm the decision and the attendance arrangement within the hour, so that I can update the tenant.

This does not establish the cause or that the socket is faulty, and it authorises no spend.
decision.rationale: This is a live electrical safety risk in an occupied home with a child: a burning smell and a warm socket face, still present after about 8.5 hours (E001, E025). Nobody qualified has inspected the socket or isolated the circuit, and the only person sent does no fixed wiring and never got in (E011, E023). The landlord holds the authority for an electrician and has not answered the 13:14 call or the 15:02 email (E020, E024). The manual says to escalate at once for a burning smell, possible electrical overheating or a vulnerable occupant, and commissioning an unapproved electrician is outside my authority. In the same turn, the tenant gets interim safety advice she has not yet had (E009, E025), and the landlord gets a second chase on a different channel (SMS), which is routine and stays with me.
decision.expectedOutcome: A duty or senior manager takes ownership tonight, reaches the landlord or uses Northbridge's emergency route, and a qualified electrician is arranged to make the socket and circuit safe. The tenant has safety guidance in the meantime.

An SMS sent to the landlord is not proof he has received or read it.

He did not go in because nobody answered and he had no clear permission to enter, so there has been no inspection and no isolation (E019, E023). We called the landlord at 13:14 and got voicemail (E020). We emailed him at 15:02 asking for an immediate decision, with no reply (E024). His only instructions so far are for the handyman to look and report, and to keep costs down. He has not approved an electrician (E006, E016, E021). 2. If he cannot be reached, decide whether Northbridge will get an electrician out under its own emergency or out-of-hours arrangements, and on what cost basis.
